name: Ukraine
headline: Ukraine: +1.8% growth in 2025, 12.7% inflation, debt 107% of GDP
sections: Ukraine is a $214 billion economy (2025), the world's 58th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +1.8% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $19K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 8.3% of GDP (2025).

Consumer prices rose 12.7% in 2025, well above typical central bank targets, down from 20.2% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 11.6% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 19.1% (2021).
Gross government debt is 107% of GDP (2025), a very high level that has risen from 61% in 2020. The general government balance is −17.6% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −16.0% of GDP (2025), a sizeable external financing need. Trade equals 77% of GDP (2025), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 0.8% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 97% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 74.7 years (2024). Population: 32.9 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
